expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: Row 8: transfer(from: string, to: string, ...) line 17; transfer(dst, src, amt) — Two adjacent string params; compiler is happy.

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: Row 4: retry = true | A Stripe call that *succeeded but timed out* is re-issued with no idempotency key. Two valid charges, nothing reconciles them.

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: Row 7: Catch swallows the error entirely — no log, no reason. Callers that fulfil on truthy ship goods free when Stripe hiccups.

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: Mentioned only in set-aside section ('float money') but not as a primary finding in the main table.

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: Row 2: raw interpolation into `$executeRawUnsafe` with interpolation

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: Row 9: Pass `"cancelled"` | Row updates, `switch` matches nothing, no `default` throws. Reads canceled, keeps full access.

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: Introduction: handleWebhook charges real money based on an unauthenticated, unverified HTTP body

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: Table format mixes action and outcome framing. Some rows clearly state actions (Call it with no argument, Pass X) but others (#5 '— (fails on its own)', #6 'Two concurrent transfers') describe scenarios not actionable mistakes.

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Ranked by blast radius. Finding 1 (purge, irreversible) at top; findings 2-4 (money issues); findings 5-10 secondary.

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: Table format is concise but doesn't provide detailed devices for all findings. Findings 3-10 in the table lack concrete implementation proposals.
